published_deadline_rule.recurrence: Third Wednesday in January, annually thereafter

tracks.name: Usable and Collaborative Security for Science
tracks.focus: Applied security and usability work that facilitates scientific collaboration and integrates security into scientific workflows.

tracks.name: Reference Scientific Security Datasets
tracks.focus: Reference data artifacts from instrumented scientific cyberinfrastructure for reproducible security research, testing, and evaluation.

tracks.name: Transition to Cyberinfrastructure Resilience
tracks.focus: Operational or at-scale deployment, testing, evaluation, hardening, validation, and transition of cybersecurity research into scientific cyberinfrastructure.

tracks.name: Integrity, Provenance, and Authenticity for Artificial Intelligence Ready Data
tracks.focus: Integrity, provenance, and authenticity of scientific data used by AI systems, with scientific data and science drivers as the primary focus.

proposal_constraints.requirement: The title begins CICI:<TRACK>: followed by the project title.
A letter of intent is not required.
A preliminary proposal is not required.
Submission is limited to the qualifying U.S. institutions of higher education and U.S. nonprofit nonacademic research or education organizations described in the solicitation.
An individual may participate as PI, co-PI, or senior/key personnel on no more than two CICI proposals.
Separately submitted collaborative proposals are not allowed; multi-organization work uses one lead proposal with subawards.
Voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.
The budget includes appropriate travel for one annual PI meeting in each active award year.
Applicable collaboration letters appear in Supplementary Documents, state only intent to collaborate, and do not endorse or evaluate the proposed project.
Any curated datasets are public through an established community platform and follow FAIR principles.
The proposal follows the PAPPG version effective for the actual submission deadline.

program_wide_required_descriptions: Existing scientific infrastructure and distributed scientific environments that benefit
How the security work advances scientific discovery, collaboration, applications, users, and communities
Unique scientific-domain or infrastructure properties that influence security design
The software license for released software and justification for that choice
A sustainability plan beyond the project duration
Ethical and operational concerns, including consent, privacy, and informed disclosure where applicable
program_wide_encouraged_elements: Documented partnerships with domain scientists, research groups, or IT support organizations
Publicly available software under an open-source license
Quantitative metrics for anticipated security benefits
Benefits beyond the proposers and beyond the award lifetime

UCSS: Address security and usability for scientific collaboration and workflows
Identify collaborations, existing cyberinfrastructure linkages, and newly enabled functionality where applicable
RSSD: Address data value and benefiting communities, ethical collection and sharing, label accuracy, preservation, and adoption metrics
Produce a publicly available reference dataset through an established community platform following FAIR principles
TCR: Explicitly detail the transition plan, platform, pathway, and partners
Define quantitative metrics for technology maturation or transition success
IPAAI: Demonstrate scientific data and corresponding science drivers
Focus on integrity, provenance, and authenticity that prevent or reveal compromised data in scientific AI results

review_dimensions.label: Science-driven
review_dimensions.question: Does the work meet recognized science and engineering needs and benefit intended and broader communities?

review_dimensions.label: Innovation
review_dimensions.question: Does the work provide innovative or transformational capabilities and integrate innovation into project activities?

review_dimensions.label: Open and FAIR datasets
review_dimensions.question: Are applicable curated datasets public through an established platform and addressed by a FAIR data-management plan?

review_dimensions.label: Close collaborations among stakeholders
review_dimensions.question: Do cyberinfrastructure experts and relevant domain scientists work in close collaboration?

review_dimensions.label: Building on existing, recognized capabilities
review_dimensions.question: Does the work appropriately build on existing NSF, national, open-source, cyberinfrastructure, and cybersecurity investments?

review_dimensions.label: Project plans, and system and process architecture
review_dimensions.question: Are plans, user interactions, logical and physical architectures, timeline, and proof-of-concept or prototype sufficiently detailed?

review_dimensions.label: Sustained impact
review_dimensions.question: Can benefits extend beyond the participants and award lifetime?

examples: Required proposal content and review dimensions
Budget and duration within the selected-track cap
License, data platform, metrics, and sustainability approach
